utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. How do things stand from the technical point of view?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right, Your Honour. I think everything is ready, technically speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Mr. Greaves, you have the floor. Who is the witness you are about to call to the stand?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness DL, and the name which you are about to see on that sheet is the correct name. Has he arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The witness is sitting at the table. He's ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: It's not immediately obvious to me. I'm sorry. I do apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness DL, I would like to ask you some questions, please, about Goran Jelisic, but first of all, can you tell Their Honours what your ethnic background is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness should first take the oath, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that's what we have to do first. I'm the one who should apologise, because I should have thought of it sooner. But I see that the legal officer of the Chamber is sending me some brain waves, and I'm well aware of what I should be doing right now. Actually, I should be asking the witness to take the oath. Mr. Registrar, what is the situation?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a slight technical problem. Let's hope it is going to be short-lived. The technical booth has just told me that things should be settled in a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: While the technical point is being resolved, can I express my concern at the fact that it appears, from the way the screen looks at the moment, that we are now ourselves even to see the face of this witness. It's one thing for the face to be distorted so far as the general public is concerned, but I had no idea, and maybe Mr. Greaves didn't either, that the face was to be distorted from all of us. It's impossible for the Trial Chamber or for the advocates to make any assessment of the witness who is entirely blanked out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, evidently. Mr. Registrar, how should we go about this? I don't understand what's happening myself, because in other cases where we had videolink conference, we could see the face of the witness. Now, in the order that was issued by the Chamber, maybe it was specified that there should be face distortion devices used, but these measures apply to the public. Think about what was done yesterday. Witnesses came into the room, their face was distorted when the images were sent to the public gallery, but that does not apply here because we, the Judges and the advocates, have to be able to see the face of the witness. If we can't see the face of the witness, anything can happen, basically. We don't know who is in front of us. We have to make sure that the protective measures are ensured, but I think the best thing to do is to suspend the hearing for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. Please be seated. Can the accused be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So as not to delay the testimony of the witness, who is right here in front of us, let us at once resume his direct examination. Then we'll go back to the issue that was raised earlier, i.e., the reason why the fourth witness which was planned to testify via videolink will not do so. But let us just continue with the present witness, Witness DK, I believe. Is that right, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour, Witness DK.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Greaves, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness DK, what was the last date in May 1992 when you saw the defendant, Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last day in 1992 was the 11th of May; that's when I saw him last.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Subsequently, did you hear from any source of any rumours concerning Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Sometime in mid-August, I heard that Goran Jelisic had been wounded and that the Serbian authorities wanted to kill him and were looking for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness DK, I would like to turn now, please, to June of this year. On the 5th of June of this year, did you go to the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Yes, I did go.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you visit somebody in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I visited the Catholic priest in a place called Vitansjneslon [phoen], which is near Karlovac, below Karlovac. We visited the priest, because he had been in Brcko before the war and the war found him in Brcko. And later on he moved, and so we went to see him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And did you have a conversation with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not getting the interpretation loudly enough. Could the volume be put up, please? Perhaps the microphone needs to be moved or something like that. A little louder, please. I can hear you now, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did he tell you something that had happened to him in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. Do you want me to tell you what he said, or shall I wait for you to ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What did he tell you about? In general terms, what was it about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about the fact that this priest -- I'm a Catholic myself, a Roman Catholic, but this priest had been in Brcko, and sometime between the 3rd and 5th of May, five masked soldiers turned up at his place and took him off to the SUP building in Brcko, the Internal Affairs secretariat and the police. That is the building where both of these organisations are. And he was held there for four days. He was kept then. They asked him for some money. Whether he didn't want to give them any money or whatever, but he spent four days in prison there. And a major, I think his name was Peric, sent him home on the seventh day and told him to bring back the money. And he was given ten minutes to take his necessary belongings and to come back to the SUP building, and this is what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Just pause there. Whilst he was detained at the SUP building, did he tell you of any threats to him that were made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He said that he was threatened, that they threatened to beat him and other things too, and I think that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did he tell you whether he had gone home for this money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said he had gone to fetch the money, escorted by a soldier, and that he came back ten minutes later, he went back to the SUP building.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Having returned to the SUP building, was he able to leave it again? Did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He couldn't leave, but he said that that particular major, Major Peric, sent him to Bijeljina, to a priest in Bijeljina, escorted by Goran Jelisic and another soldier nicknamed Sok. So these two escorted him to Bijeljina, and they thought that they would liquidate him on the way there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did he give any account to you as to how he was treated by Goran Jelisic during the course of that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He told us everything as things evolved and that he was at the house of the Major. Goran Jelisic went out to have a fruit juice. He said he didn't want any, and the priest sat as a co-driver. And I forget to say that this man nicknamed Sok had a Kalishnikoff automatic rifle with him, and they went towards Bijeljina. Goran Jelisic addressed him as "Father." His conduct towards him was extremely proper, and he transferred him -- he placed him in the care of the priest in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And did he have any complaint at all about the conduct of Goran Jelisic or, indeed, the other man towards him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he had no complaints and said he was surprised by their conduct, that they were very proper towards him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness DK. Would you be so kind as to wait there and answer any questions which are put to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The Prosecutor will now ask you a few questions, Witness DK. I'm sure you've been informed of that. Mr. Nice, the floor is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just dealing with the priest, the priest was a Catholic priest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was, in Brcko, before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You saw him in the summer of this year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. He's in Brcko again now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He's fit and well and able to travel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's healthy, he's well, he's able to travel, but he did not want to promise us that he would give any statement, make any written statement or anything else, because the laws of the church forbid it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Who is the "us" that you referred to in that last answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we -- we asked whether he would make a written statement or testify in court, any court, in an office, to the International Court or this distinguished Tribunal, and he said, no, because it is a long procedure and he would have to ask permission from the church authorities. I don't know what they are called.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You say "we." Have you been involved in gathering the evidence for this defendant that you use the word "we"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked by a lawyer that I should hear where that priest is, and I heard from my colleague, who has some in-laws who -- and they said that the priest was in Slunj, or Vitanci, or whatever the place is called near Slunj, and so we went to visit him; that is to say, I, myself, and Mr. Londrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And so it's you and Mr. Londrovic who have been trying to get the evidence, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Why are you so involved in the Defence of Jelisic when you only met him for two days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not taking part in the Defence. I just wish to state the truth about Jelisic as I know it, and I am telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You saw the man for about two days, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: About four, about four days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I repeat: Why are you so involved in his Defence if you only knew the man for a few, you say, four days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that the family's in our neighbourhood. I didn't know what Goran Jelisic was doing; nor did he tell me. If Goran Jelisic has these people on his conscience, then he should be held responsible. But if anybody forced Goran Jelisic to perform the acts he did, then it would be necessary for Goran Jelisic to state those names so that those people could be held accountable.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And as you understand it, Witness DK, people did force Jelisic to do these killings; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do consider that somebody ordered him to perform those acts. And Goran is a young man. He probably didn't understand. Of course, nobody must take anybody's life. That is my opinion, and I shall always stand by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm going to come back and give you a chance to tell us more detail of the pressure that was put on Jelisic a little later.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May we have a necessary private session to deal with matters of identification? I'm going to ask the witness to look at a map, but I hope -- there's nobody in the public gallery. If the matter can be dealt with swiftly, so much the better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but whatever the case, we should go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge Riad. We're now going back into open session, but, sir, you are still benefiting from the protective measures you've been benefiting from since the very beginning of your testimony. Now Judge Rodrigues will ask you a number of questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness DK, you have just told my colleague, Judge Riad, that you had seen Mr. Jelisic during four days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. I seem to remember hearing you saying that on the very first day, on the 8th of May, you had spent about 10 to 15 minutes with him. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right. Our meeting was never longer when he came, stopped by with the girl. It wasn't more than 10 to 15 minutes, a coffee and a walk. He had his business to attend to. I'm a pensioner. That was how it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you spent about 10 to 15 minutes with him, and is that the amount of time you spent with him every day during those four days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: About that long, 15 to 20 minutes. He never stayed longer, because he walked around with his girlfriend. They went to Bijeljina. It was May. They walked around. Unfortunately, it was a day of sunshine and flowers, but Brcko had a day of mourning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also seem to remember you saying that the last time you saw Mr. Jelisic was May the 11th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, between the 10th and 11th of May, I saw him. You know, seven years have gone by since then. And as I said, on that occasion, he was nervous and sad, if I can say that, and not in a good mood, and that's when we had the talks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After that particular date, after May the 11th, have you ever had the opportunity to meet Mr. Jelisic again or did you never see him after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never met him again. I never saw him again, but I heard what I told you about in August, that they were looking for him and wanted to kill him and that he was wounded. But he can tell you about that, because I didn't actually see it, so I don't want to claim anything I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So according to you, Mr. Jelisic did not come back on the 12th, on the 13th, or on the 14th or the 15th, he did not come back because he followed your advice and escaped and ran away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that's precisely what happened. And he should have listened to my advice, because who can be allowed to kill people, I ask you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you are well aware of the fact that on the 18th of May, on the 20th of May, he did kill people. But okay. I have another question for you. No, sorry, I don't have another question for you. That will be all. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Rodrigues. I will have one or two questions --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Good afternoon to you too. It was your niece who came with Goran Jelisic? I'm not sure I understood you fully well. Was it your niece which came to visit you with Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: My nephew's daughter. I am a sort of uncle to her father, and she called me "Uncle."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you ever see that young woman again? Have you seen her since all these events have taken place? What has become of her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 20th or 25th of May, I don't know the exact date, she was no longer in Brcko, and I don't know where she is now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you are very close to your family. Have you never asked any of your relatives what had become of her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gentlemen Judges, her father and mother moved to another republic as well. They didn't remain where they had lived, so who can I ask?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A lot of events have taken place since that particular time, Witness DK. Since then, you have learned that Goran Jelisic, whom you trusted during four days, four days during which he was about 100 metres away from your house, since these events you have learned that he has killed a number of people. He goes around with your niece. He calls you "Uncle." You've learned since then that he's said himself that he was guilty of a number of crimes. Have you not been shaken by all this? We've been talking about this as if it was something quite normal. You've been describing it as a very objective event, whereas it's something that's quite unusual, quite dramatic. Have you not questioned the fact that you have been quite blind to reality? Does that not affect what you have told us, Witness DK? You don't wonder about anything you've said or your behaviour at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, he did not tell me, even on that day, "I have killed so many people." He just said that pressure had been exerted on him to kill. And my organism knows best, my body knows best about that, and that had I -- Goran Jelisic was not my friend. But I do, nonetheless, wish to state what I know and what I consider to be the truth, and I have taken the oath. This is not the first time I have taken the oath. I have taken the oath in Brcko several times when I worked on a jury and so on, so I know what it means to take the oath. But had Goran said to me, "Good day, hello, I've killed one man," then I would say, "Well, we have nothing to talk about." But what he, in fact, told me was that the authorities were bringing pressure to bear on him to kill. First of all, he said, "They are making me do dirty things." I asked him, "What dirty things," and he said, "To kill." I said, "Goran, you should flee, because you must not kill."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that, and I was about to say, "Dear colleague, I understand what you're saying." But to take upon you to work as Mr. Londrovic asks you to work, to try and do things for Mr. Jelisic, that's something I cannot understand from a psychological point of view. I do, you know, pay homage to your courage. I do thank you for coming all the way to The Hague, but you have been acting as a man going around trying to find positive testimonies in favour of Mr. Jelisic, a man who has publicly recognised that he had killed a number of individuals, and that's something I can't quite understand. Then you tell us that you sometimes act as a judge. So that's something else. Maybe we don't see being a judge as -- or we don't agree on what a judge is. That's why I ask you that particular question. I was just wondering what kind of witness you were, in fact. I think Judge Rodrigues has another question he wishes to put to you, because maybe my questions have triggered a number of thoughts in his mind. But that's what I'm interested in, Witness DK. I'm trying to understand what exactly, who you are. Actually, can I put that question to you? Would you accept Goran Jelisic marrying your niece today? Is he the ideal son-in-law that you've met during four days and to whom you've offered coffee at a time when everybody was afraid of everything. And you told us that 100 metres away from your house you could see the refrigerated trucks coming and going. I'm well aware that seven years have gone by since what has happened, but you come now here today and tell us about now nice a man Mr. Jelisic is, and you've told us how you've worked for Mr. Londrovic, how you've gone and try -- positive testimony on behalf of Mr. Londrovic. I don't have a question for you really, but I don't think we have the same job as judges. Now Judge Rodrigues has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness DK, I'm sorry to put another question to you. A moment ago I was a bit disorganised but now I feel I can put this question to you. It seems that you told us an uncle and an aunt of Mr. Jelisic's lived right next door to you. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not next to my house but in the next street. His Uncle Milorad and his Aunt Borka. Borka is a teacher and Milorad is a -- and I'll tell what happened to Milorad later on if you permit me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry for cutting in. How? How did you know that these people were the uncle and the aunt of Mr. Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Jelisic told -- Goran Jelisic -- I apologise -- told me that when he came to my yard for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So before May the 8th, you had never talked with these people about Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which people do you mean? Which people? Talked to which people?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The uncle and the aunt of Goran Jelisic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew them, and I would give his aunt a lift, because she's a teacher near where I lived. So I knew Milorad and Borka, but I didn't know Goran himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. But you've learned from Mr. Jelisic that these people you knew were, in fact, his aunt and uncle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that from Goran the first day he came to my yard and introduced himself. I heard "Jelisic," and I asked whether he was any relation to the Jelisics that I knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it was only then that you were able to establish the link between these two individuals and the person who was standing in front of you? It was only then that you became aware of the fact that they were, in fact, his uncle and his aunt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another question for you, Witness DK.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go ahead. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since it seemed to be a difficult thing to do for Mr. Londrovic, being a Serb and an Orthodox, to go and have an interview with this priest who was a Catholic and a Croat, why was it easier for Mr. Londrovic, who is a Serb and who is an Orthodox, to go and have an interview with you, who are a Catholic and a Croat? You are in the very same position as the priest. The priest is a Croat and a Catholic, and he is not interviewed by a Serb and an Orthodox, but you are a Croat and a Catholic and it's much easier for that Serb and Orthodox, for Mr. Londrovic, to go and have an interview with you. How can you explain this? Have you understood my question, in fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've understood the question, but I am retired, I have lots of time, and I'd help anybody arrive at the truth. And my neighbour also has a relative of his who's a priest, and he said that this priest, Danic Pero, was in Slunj; that is to say, the village near Slunj. And I see no reason for not going there with anybody if I was asked to go nicely. And it doesn't matter if I'm a Croat and Londrovic is a Serb. If we're men and human beings, we can talk like human beings. And Mr. Londrovic struck me as a very fine man and lawyer. I know that he was president of the court in Bijeljina at one time. And can I put something right that the Judge said a moment ago, that we were judges. No, I was on the jury. You know what a jury is. You have the judges and you have the jury, women and men of the jury elected territorially and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry to interrupt you, Witness DK.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you already had links with Mr. Londrovic? You already knew him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him by sight. As to the legal affairs, I'm not a legal man myself. I'm an accountant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was there any particular relation between Mr. Londrovic and Mr. Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. They could not have seen each other in Brcko. Whether they saw each other here or somewhere else, I don't know. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness DK.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Greaves?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: My client is feeling unwell. May he leave the court, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, actually, I think that everybody will leave the court, Mr. Greaves. I think that we will put an end to the hearing. But, of course, your client may leave at once, but we will suspend the hearing and resume our work tomorrow morning at 10.00.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. That's right, Your Honour, tomorrow morning at 10.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jelisic, do you want to say something? You're feeling unwell? Do you want to say something?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I apologise for having to leave every hour. I have taken five pills so far. I do apologise, but I really am feeling poorly, and if I may, I'd like to go out. I will do everything in my power not to stay out for too long and to come to these proceedings regularly, but if I may be excused at this particular time I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you're not feeling well, if you're sick, Mr. Jelisic, you will benefit from medical care at the detention unit, and I don't think that whenever you have felt sick we, the Judges, have refused you all the medical help you are entitled to. Don't remain standing. You may leave the courtroom. As I said a moment ago, we will end the hearing and it will be resumed tomorrow morning at 10.00. Witness DK, thank you for coming. You may return to your country now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
